description:
FILED s460ap (agent AP, round 17).  #873 shipped its other two write slots
(assignment, `open`); this is the third, and it is left OPEN because a
COMPILE-TIME die is provably wrong for it.

WHAT PERL DOES.  perl decides at RUN TIME whether an s/// or tr/// against a
read-only target dies, and perl-tests/tr.t asserts the exceptions BY NAME.
Probed 5.40.3 after `'abcdef' =~ /(bcd)/`, `eval { $1 =~ OP }`:

    tr/abcd//         count, empty repl        no error   tr.t:748 "explicit read-only count"
    tr/abcd/abcd/     replacement identical    no error   tr.t:752 "implicit read-only count"
    tr/abcd//c        complement, empty repl   no error
    tr///             empty search             no error
    tr/a-z/A-Z/r      /r returns a copy        no error
    tr/abcd/abcd/r    /r                       no error
    tr/a-z/A-Z/       modifies                 DIES
    tr/a-z//d         deletes                  DIES
    tr/a-z//s         squeezes                 DIES
    tr/abcd/ab/       short replacement        DIES
    s/b/z/            matches                  DIES
    s/zzz/q/          NO MATCH                 no error   <-- the run-time half
    s/b/z/r           /r                       no error
    m/b/              a read                   no error

tr.t rows 631 and 639 are the same rule in prose: "harmless if explicitly not
updating" / "harmless if implicitly not updating".  A compile-time die on
`rhs_is_subst_tr && capture target` was WRITTEN in s460ap and REVERTED: it
moved perl-tests/tr.t in corpus-diff, i.e. it would have broken four blessed
rows.  Do not retry it.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS, located.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp already has BOTH sites,
and both already fire exactly when a write is needed -- which is exactly where
perl croaks:

    s///:  (if (p-box-p string-box)
               (setf (p-box-value string-box) result ...)
               (warn "Cannot modify non-boxed value in s///"))
           ... guarded by `(and (stringp result) (plusp count))`, i.e. ONLY on
           a match -- which is precisely the `s/zzz/q/` exception.
    tr///: the same shape, guarded by `(when (string/= result str) ...)`, i.e.
           only when the transliteration actually changes the target -- which
           is precisely the tr/abcd// and tr/abcd/abcd/ exceptions, and even
           finer than perl's compile-time OPpTRANS_IDENTICAL flag.

So the SHAPE is: turn those two `warn`s into `(%p-readonly-modification)` --
the same helper #873's two slots use, so the text is perl's byte for byte and
it is trappable.  NO compiler change is needed for the capture case.

WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY IS -- the audit, not the edit.  The question is what
ELSE reaches those two sites with a NON-BOX target, because today they warn and
carry on and turning that into a death could kill a program perl accepts.
Candidates to enumerate before flipping: a raw (unpromoted) array or hash
element under the s455 boxed-aggregates model, a `p-gethash`/`p-aref` result
taken in rvalue context, an @_ element, a literal (`"abc" =~ s/a/b/`, which
perl rejects at COMPILE time with "Can't modify constant item", so a run-time
death there is closer than a warning).  Instrument the two sites over the
sweep + the companion + the cpan board and read what arrives; if the only
arrivals are shapes perl also refuses, flip both warns unconditionally.  If
not, the capture case needs to be marked -- and note that #874 is the reason a
STDERR WARNING is not an acceptable resting place either.

BAR: the 14-row table above vs perl; perl-tests/tr.t rows 631/639/748/752
still passing; the two `Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t` #873 rows extended with the
s///-and-tr/// spellings; full sweep (the sites are on every s/// path).

SHIPPED s461ar (agent AR, round 18), exactly as the task sketched it: the two
`warn`s in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp became %p-readonly-modification, and NO compiler
change was needed.

THE AUDIT the task asked for, done by probe and then by sweep.  Probed 5.40.3
vs ./runpcl, every shape that can reach the two sites with a NON-BOX target:
  * the 14-row table in this task -- PCL now matches perl's DIES/no-error
    column on all of it, including the run-time half (`s/zzz/q/` no match, any
    `/r`, `tr` with an empty or identical replacement).
  * `$&` and the rest of the capture family reach the same sites and now agree.
  * the ORDINARY element shapes DO NOT reach them and were unmoved: `$a[0] =~
    s///`, `$h{k} =~ s///`, an @_ element, a foreach alias, a `\$a[1]` deref, a
    map body, `$_`, and a postfix-for alias -- all identical to perl before and
    after, no warning, no death.
  * FOUR shapes still accept what perl refuses, because they never reach the
    sites (PCL boxes the value first): `$+`, a foreach over a LITERAL list,
    sort's `$a`, and `$_ =~ s/// for (LIST)`.  Filed as task #936 -- the fix
    there is a read-only MARK on the box, shared with #873 and
    %p-array-readonly-p, not a third write site.
  * a literal or a sub return (`"abc" =~ s///`, `f() =~ s///`) is a perl
    COMPILE error, so it is out of this task's scope either way.

BARS: full perl-tests sweep GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18342 (+0) -- tr.t's rows
631/639/748/752 still passing, and tr.t's only three failures are the
unrelated \N{} ones; gate 191/6461; companion op/ + re/ legs; guard
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t gains a 12-row both_agree table (plan 8 -> 9),
inverse-verified on a 33a71c9 worktree.
subject: `$1 =~ s///` and `$1 =~ tr///` do not die: the runtime's two write sites WARN where perl croaks (#873's third slot, boundary measured)
